title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS - (c) IS DUE TODAY AND IS STILL UNRUN AT THE THIRD FIRE; (a) DUE TOMORROW; (b) AND (e) DUE SEP 12 - PLUS A FOURTH MISS FOUND IN THIS REPORT'S OWN SOURCE
bullets.summary: Not news; this report's open decisions, carried from the 06:04 and 10:00 fires. (a) misalignment / MCP incident log - DUE TOMORROW SEP 11, no longer a design problem: Anthropic's Compliance API returns Cowork and Claude Code session transcripts with MCP tool-call content, per-message IDs and timestamps, so (a) is build-or-buy (Enterprise tier, or hand-roll the same five-field record). (b) Entra's four MCP controls as a config script - DUE SEP 12, and bullet 3 finally gives it a measured baseline instead of a vendor claim. (c) /skill-doctor across the ~130-skill corpus - DUE TODAY, runnable since Sep 4 in v2.1.261, gated only by being a Claude Code terminal command while the corpus loads into Cowork; bullet 5 supplies the load-order its output should produce. (e) cadence-cost measurement before the Sep 14 Claude Code limit change - DUE SEP 12, re-priced this morning against the 0.025x cache-read rate. Also standing and unactioned: the built-in-browser split (credentialed work stays in the attached Chrome, measurement work moves to the isolated profile). NEW THIS FIRE: bullet 2 is a same-day miss from a source both earlier fires read.
bullets.how: YES. Two facts this fire adds. First the clock: (c) was due at 00:00, three fires have now written about it, and no number from /skill-doctor exists - the 06:04 fire said the only honest measure of the next fire is whether it reports a number or a seventh reason, and this is the seventh reason. Second, and more useful: this morning's fix for our staleness was a SETTINGS fix (raise effort so retrieval fires). Bullet 2 shows that fix would not have caught Harvey, because retrieval DID fire - the item was inside a roundup both fires read and neither picked. That is a fourth failure mechanism, and it is the first one that no configuration change addresses.

bullets.title: THE DAY'S LEAD - THE VERTICAL AGENT OPERATOR WAS PRICED AT $15.6B YESTERDAY AND WE READ THE PAGE IT WAS ON: HARVEY RAISED $550M ON >$400M ARR, AND ITS MOAT IS THAT IT OWNS THE BENCHMARK AND SHIPS A MODEL THE CLIENT KEEPS
bullets.summary: Harvey closed $550M on Sep 9 at a reported $15.6B valuation (some outlets print $15.5B; Bloomberg carries $15.6B - discrepancy printed, both are company-reported at announcement), co-led by Lightspeed and Diffusion, a new firm founded by longtime backer Kris Fredrickson, with Sequoia, Kleiner Perkins, a16z, Coatue, Goldman Sachs Alternatives and GIC returning and Sapphire and Whale Rock new. ARR is past $400M, valuation up more than 40% in six months, and 80% of the Am Law 100 plus five Fortune 10 companies are customers. The two products behind the round matter more than the round. HARVEY LAB, launched May 6 and OPEN-SOURCED, is a long-horizon legal agent benchmark: 1,200+ tasks across 24 practice areas graded against 75,000+ expert-written rubric criteria under ALL-PASS grading - a task counts only if every criterion passes, on the stated rationale that a deal memo catching eight of ten material risks is not 80% useful. Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral and DeepMind engaged with it. HARVEY TENET, announced Aug 20, is a post-trained OPEN-WEIGHT model on a Kimi K3 base built with Fireworks, state-of-the-art on LAB Contracts and second across broader LAB. The positioning line in the raise is 'build and own their intelligence at scale,' and the coverage frames it as a model that keeps client documents in firm control.
bullets.how: YES, and it is the sharpest competitive read this report has produced for PRAGMA - which makes the way we found it the second story. Harvey is the vertical AI operator, executed: one industry, deep workflow, sold to the people who already own the work. Set it against our operator pitch and three differences are structural, not budgetary. (1) HARVEY OWNS THE MEASURING STICK. It built the benchmark its category is judged by, open-sourced it, and got five frontier labs to engage - so the standard of 'good legal agent' is defined on its terms. PRAGMA sells an AAIR score on a registry we run; that is the same move at a fraction of the scale, and the lesson is that the benchmark only becomes a moat when OTHER people use it to grade THEMSELVES. That is the question to ask of the AAIR registry this quarter. (2) ALL-PASS GRADING IS OUR RENDER GATE, SOLD AS A PRODUCT. 'Eight of ten material risks is not 80% useful' is verbatim the logic of interrogate-the-render and gate-measures-defects-not-beauty. We treat it as internal hygiene; Harvey made it the headline of a benchmark. Any client-facing PRAGMA or VironBox score should grade all-pass and say so. (3) THE CLIENT KEEPS THE INTELLIGENCE. Open-weight, in-firm, documents under client control - that answers the objection every high-ticket buyer raises about dependence on an agency. Ledger and Keystone should price what our equivalent is, because 'we run your agents' and 'you own the thing we built' are different businesses with different margins. Now the miss. Clay's $115M went into the 06:04 fire from the Sep 9 funding roundup; HARVEY'S $550M WAS IN THE SAME ROUNDUP, five times larger, and closer to our thesis than Clay is - and two fires passed over it. Harvey appeared in an earlier scan on Sep 3, so it is not an unknown name.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTION (b) FINALLY HAS A MEASURED BASELINE INSTEAD OF A VENDOR CLAIM: A SCAN OF 21,000 INTERNET-FACING MCP SERVERS FOUND 91.8% WITH NO AUTHENTICATION AT ALL AND 687 TOOL INSTANCES EXPOSING SHELL EXECUTION WITH NO ACCESS CONTROL
bullets.summary: 'Exposed by Design' (arXiv 2608.00150) discovered more than 21,000 MCP server instances on the public internet through passive discovery across eleven sources, confirmed 640 as production servers, and dynamically audited 414 of them with a 34-module framework covering ten MCP-specific vulnerability classes. Findings: 68 reportable vulnerabilities including SQL injection, SSRF against cloud metadata services, prompt template injection and path traversal via cursor manipulation; 91.8% of servers with no authentication at all; 687 tool instances exposing shell execution with no access control; and 41.6% of servers vanishing between scan runs within three days. Corroborating figures circulating separately: roughly 8.5% of servers using OAuth, and autonomous agents accounting for more than 12% of reported AI breaches in HiddenLayer's 2026 threat report. Source-quality note stated plainly: 2608.00150 was submitted Jul 31, not in the last 24h, and it is carried under the weekly backward-sweep rule this report adopted on Sep 9; the aggregator statistics around it are secondary and are flagged as such.
bullets.how: YES, and it converts (b) from a config chore into a scoped audit with a number attached. Yesterday Deadbugz gave us the attack; the Entra controls gave us the levers; what was missing was any sense of how bad the ambient surface is, and 91.8% unauthenticated is the answer. Three concrete consequences. First, the shadow-server inventory in (b) is not hypothetical hygiene - the base rate says an arbitrary MCP server we have not vetted is far more likely than not to be running with no auth, so 'discover what is connected' is the highest-value of the four controls and should run first. Second, 687 shell-execution instances with no access control names the exact class our own credential routing is exposed to, and it argues for pinning transport and protocol version (2026-07-28) rather than trusting a server's own posture. Third, and least comfortable: 41.6% of audited servers DISAPPEARED WITHIN THREE DAYS. A dependency that evaporates in seventy-two hours cannot be a load-bearing part of a client deliverable, which is a procurement rule we do not currently have - anything in the B9 or ANS pipeline that calls a third-party MCP server needs a named fallback. Do not overstate the paper: it audits internet-EXPOSED servers, which skews toward the careless, and most of our surface is first-party or vendor-hosted. The number is a ceiling on ambient risk, not a measurement of ours - which is precisely why (b) should produce OUR number this week.

bullets.title: SALESFORCE IS IN TALKS TO BUY AN AI CUSTOMER-RESEARCH AGENT FOR $2B AT ROUGHLY 67x REVENUE - THE PRISM ADJACENCY, AND A PRICE ON 'THE AGENT DOES THE RESEARCH'
bullets.summary: Salesforce is reportedly in preliminary talks to acquire Listen Labs for around $2B. Listen Labs, founded 2023, automates qualitative customer research end to end: its AI interviewers design studies, recruit participants from a global network, and conduct the interviews themselves - work that traditionally needs human moderators and weeks of scheduling. Reported financials: roughly $30M annualised revenue against a ~$2B price, i.e. about 67x revenue, and roughly a 4x markup on a $500M valuation eight months ago. Named customers include Microsoft, Canva, Anthropic and Sweetgreen. It would be Salesforce's fourth AI-related acquisition of 2026. Source-quality note: these are TALKS reported by the press and explicitly may not result in a deal; the revenue figure and the prior valuation are reported, not audited. Nothing here is confirmed.
bullets.how: MAYBE - unconfirmed, and not a tool we would adopt, but it prices a motion Prism already performs. Prism's job is alt-data and demand signal: foot traffic, spend, demographics, institutional voids. Listen Labs sells the qualitative half of the same question - not what the market did, but why - executed by agents rather than moderators, and the market is putting 67x revenue on it. Two readings that do not agree. The one that flatters us: the buyer is Salesforce, which means agentic research is being absorbed into the CRM stack as a feature rather than surviving as a standalone category, and PRAGMA's bet that the OPERATOR rather than the point tool is the durable unit gets modest support. The one that stings: 67x on $30M means the market is paying for the WORKFLOW REPLACED, not the software shipped, and Listen Labs replaced a legible, expensive, previously-human line item. That is the valuation logic PRAGMA should be able to state on one line for each client and currently cannot - which of their line items did the operator delete, and what did it cost before. Filed maybe because it is unconfirmed and changes no build. The honest actions are two names on Scout's watch list and one question for Ledger: what is our replaced-cost number per client.

bullets.title: THE LOAD-ORDER STANDING ACTION (c) SHOULD OUTPUT ALREADY EXISTS AS A PUBLISHED ARCHITECTURE: HOT MEMORY ALWAYS LOADED, DOMAIN SPECIALISTS PER TASK, COLD MEMORY RETRIEVED ON DEMAND
bullets.summary: 'Codified Context: Infrastructure for AI Agents in a Complex Codebase' (arXiv 2602.20478) proposes a three-tier context architecture, each tier with a distinct loading strategy and update frequency: HOT MEMORY - the constitution, always loaded; DOMAIN SPECIALISTS - agents invoked per task; and COLD MEMORY - the knowledge base, retrieved on demand. It sits alongside 'Agentic Context Engineering' (2510.04618), which optimises context both offline as system prompts and online as agent memory and reports gains of +10.6% on agent tasks and +8.6% on finance over strong baselines, and 'Harness Engineering for Agentic AI Coding Tools' (2602.14690). Source-quality note, stated because the task asks for papers from this week and these are not: 2602.20478 is a February 2026 preprint and 2510.04618 is older still; both are carried under the backward-sweep rule, and no agent-architecture paper published this week surfaced as significant on this pass.
bullets.how: YES, because it closes the loop the last three fires opened and it makes (c) a smaller job than we have been treating it as. Yesterday's arXiv 2603.09619 gave us the WORD - economy - for the ~130-skill context tax. This morning the MCP roadmap confirmed the tax is STRUCTURAL, not a sign we over-collected, and named the protocol-side fix progressive discovery. This paper supplies the SHAPE on our side of the line, and our corpus already sorts into it cleanly: hot memory is the locked rules and the always-true operating facts (the V4 dashboard path, the deploy targets, the browser rules); domain specialists are the per-client and per-pipeline skills that should load only when a task names them; cold memory is the reference mass - the render libraries, the site architectures, the historical records like the 3ds-max kill list - that should be retrieved, not resident. So (c)'s deliverable is now specifiable in one sentence before it runs: not a prune list and not a guilt exercise, but an ECONOMY NUMBER plus each skill assigned to one of three tiers. That is the output that feeds (e)'s Sep 12 cadence-cost measurement, because context resident on every turn is the input to the cost model. Do not over-read the papers - a preprint proves nothing, ACE's +10.6% is on its own benchmarks and not our corpus. The value is that we no longer have to invent a taxonomy to run an audit that was due at midnight.

praxis_lesson: Three fires today produced a settings diagnosis, a mechanism, and now a fourth failure mode that the settings fix cannot touch. This morning's lead was Anthropic's own documentation explaining our staleness - Fable 5.1 ANSWERS FROM MEMORY MORE OFTEN AT LOW EFFORT, and Cowork defaults to Medium where Claude Code defaults to High - and the prescribed fix was to raise effort so retrieval fires. That fix is right and should still be made. IT WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT TODAY'S MISS. Harvey raised $550M at $15.6B on >$400M ARR, and the item was sitting in the SAME Sep 9 funding roundup from which the 06:04 fire lifted Clay's $115M - retrieval fired, the page was read, the bigger and more relevant item was passed over. Line up the week now: Cognition (same day, inside a declared boundary), HiddenLayer (seven days, no backward sweep), /skill-doctor (four days, wrong version credited), Harvey (same day, same page, not selected). The first three are retrieval failures and the settings change addresses them. THE FOURTH IS A SELECTION FAILURE, AND NO CONFIGURATION CHANGE FIXES SELECTION. The correction is specific and cheap: when a source is a LIST - a funding roundup, a changelog, a release index - do not take the first relevant item and move on; enumerate every item in it and rank by relevance to the three businesses before writing. One pass over a page already open. And state the ranking failure honestly, because it is the more embarrassing half: we chose a $115M GTM tool over a $550M vertical operator that owns its category's open-source benchmark and ships a model its clients keep - which is PRAGMA's own thesis, executed, at scale, by someone else. The reason that matters more than the miss: Harvey's three moves are all available to us at our size - grade all-pass and say so, get someone else to use your benchmark on themselves, and let the client own what you built. Keystone should read bullet 2 before the next positioning conversation. Finally, the number that has not changed since midnight. Standing action (c) was due today. Three fires have now written about it, this one has handed it a ready-made three-tier taxonomy from bullet 5 so it no longer needs designing, and the corpus is still unmeasured. (a) is due tomorrow and is one decision, not a design. THE NEXT FIRE EITHER REPORTS A NUMBER OR IT REPORTS AN EIGHTH REASON.
